title: Thinking Orbs, Grid Lanes, Text Dissolves, Jelly Press & Lifeline
description: Five live drops: dotted agent-state orbs, the grid-lanes tab-order trap, cursor-driven text dissolves, soft-body jelly buttons, and a wheel-scrubbed timeline.

drops.title: Thinking Orbs
drops.description: Six agent loading states drawn as dots on rotating 3D orbits — plain 2D canvas arcs, no WebGL, no filters.
drops.concept: thinking-orbs went from zero to ~2k stars in three weeks by replacing the generic spinner with loaders that name the work: working, searching, weaving, shaping, breathing, listening. Each state is a point cloud on a unit sphere or ring, rotated per frame and depth-sorted so the far side dims and shrinks. Every orb on the page shares one rAF clock and pauses when offscreen or when the tab is hidden.

interaction.mouse: hover any orb card to lift it; the debug panel retunes the hero orb live
interaction.click: click a state card to promote that state to the hero orb
interaction.touch: tap a state card — orbs are non-interactive elsewhere and keep animating
interaction.keyboard: range inputs in the parameter panel are keyboard-operable

drops.title: Grid Lanes & the Tab-Order Trap
drops.description: The real display:grid-lanes placement algorithm with a live flow-tolerance dial and a drawn tab path that turns red where masonry breaks WCAG 2.4.3.
drops.concept: Safari shipped Grid Lanes (the artist formerly known as CSS masonry) and Matuzovic immediately pointed out that it fails focus order by default: items go into whichever lane sits closest to the start edge, so the DOM order and the visual order diverge. This drop re-derives that placement algorithm — including the flow-tolerance threshold and the tie-break that resumes from the lane after the last one filled — and draws the tab path straight over the board so you can watch focus run backwards up the page.
drops.source: Manuel Matuzovic — “Your Grid Lanes will likely fail WCAG 2.4.3”

interaction.mouse: drag the columns / flow-tolerance / items / gap sliders and watch the board repack
interaction.click: toggle the tab path, infinite tolerance, unpack-while-focused, and shuffled heights
interaction.touch: tap the toggle pills; the boards reflow on resize
interaction.keyboard: click a card then hold Tab — every red edge in the path is a jump you just felt

drops.title: Cursor-Driven Text Dissolves
drops.description: An ASCII lens sampling real ink density, a cipher decrypting under a flickering wavefront, and glyph rain lighting the copy it falls through.
drops.concept: canvas-ui is the html-in-canvas component library that took over the timeline this month; three of its most-shared components are text effects. Here they are rebuilt without the experimental API: the paragraph is rasterised once to an offscreen canvas, per-cell ink coverage becomes a density ramp for the ASCII lens, and the same character grid drives a per-cell decrypt progress and a set of falling glyph streams. Leave the pointer alone and a ghost cursor keeps all three alive.
drops.source: DavidHDev/canvas-ui — Asciify, Decrypt Reveal, Glyph Rain

interaction.mouse: move across any panel — the lens, the decrypt front and the rain surge all follow the pointer
interaction.click: no click needed; the parameter panel retunes cell size, lens radius, flicker and rain speed
interaction.touch: drag a finger across a panel; idle for a moment and the ghost cursor takes over
interaction.keyboard: sliders are focusable and step the effect parameters

drops.title: Jelly Press
drops.description: Buttons built from a spring-coupled membrane ring with pressure-based volume preservation — press one spot and the rest genuinely bulges.
drops.concept: jelly-org/ui shipped 40+ components whose surfaces are simulated rather than transformed: a closed ring of points around a rounded rectangle, structural springs along the membrane, shape memory pulling back to rest, and an internal pressure term that fights any change in enclosed area. Press it and the deformation is real — the area meter dips, the sides swell, and the whole thing wobbles to rest before the physics loop puts itself to sleep.

interaction.mouse: press and hold to dent the membrane, drag while held to move the dent around
interaction.click: click any control — the toggle commits its state on release
interaction.touch: tap or drag; touch-action is disabled on the controls so the press lands
interaction.keyboard: Tab to a control and hit Space or Enter for a scripted poke

drops.title: Lifeline
drops.description: A timeline that scrubs sideways on the wheel and hands the scroll back at both ends, with hover-bloom media and a lightbox.
drops.concept: evilrabbit's lifeline is a shadcn-registry timeline for stories that unfold over time, and its best idea is the scroll contract: the component captures the wheel to scrub horizontally, then releases it the moment you reach either boundary so the page keeps scrolling. Rebuilt here dependency-free with a drawn-in rail, year ticks, hover-bloom media cards, a lightbox, arrow-key stepping, and a vertical fallback under 720px.

interaction.mouse: wheel over the rail to scrub, drag to throw it, hover an event to bloom its media
interaction.click: click an event to open its lightbox; click the backdrop or Close to dismiss
interaction.touch: drag horizontally on the rail; under 720px the whole thing flips to a vertical list
interaction.keyboard: ← → step between events, Enter opens the lightbox, Esc closes it
